sections.heading: Overview & objectives
sections.body_markdown:
A member of staff needs to add, edit, find and retire the printing products that customers browse and order on the storefront. This is the admin half of the *Product Catalog (Admin to Storefront)* journey; the storefront half — how those products are browsed, searched and filtered by customers — was tested and documented separately.

The admin product catalogue is the single source of truth for everything the business sells. A product that saves with the wrong price, the wrong slug, or no name at all does not stay an admin-panel problem: it appears in the storefront listing, in search results, and in an order total. That is why this run was scoped to be exhaustive about validation rather than to demonstrate a happy path — every field's rules, every distinct error message, every control on the product list, and — in a follow-up pass documented here — every combination of clearing a required field against every way the form can be saved, were exercised against the real application and the real FastAPI backend.

**Result: 91 recorded steps, 91 passing, 0 failing.** Seven real defects were found and fixed across two passes; two further findings — one about what 'Save as Draft' is allowed to do, and a data-integrity issue in how photo removal interacts with the save guards — are surfaced below for a human decision rather than patched unilaterally.

sections.heading: Feature description & business logic
sections.body_markdown:
The catalogue lives at `/products`, backed by `GET /admin/products` and rendered through a shared `DataTable`. Each row shows the product's name and category, a status badge, the 'From' price, and the created date, with a row menu offering Edit and Delete. A toolbar carries a search box, a status filter and a category filter — all three now backed by real query parameters — and a footer paginates at 20 rows per page.

Creating or editing a product uses one form (`ProductForm`) in two modes, decided by whether a product was loaded. It is divided into eight collapsible sections — Basic Information, Customization, Images & Video, Print Specifications, Pricing Tiers, Turnaround Options, Inventory and SEO. Two sidebar buttons submit it, and — as of this run — both genuinely validate before doing anything: **Publish Product** saves with `status: active`, **Save as Draft** saves with `status: draft`. The same form is reused for both create and edit, so the button reads *Publish Product* on a new product and *Save Changes* on an existing one; on an existing product, Save as Draft does not create a separate draft copy — it patches the live record's own status back to `draft`, unpublishing it.

Several rules are enforced on the way out, and this run's second pass specifically tested every one of them against all four combinations of (create or update an existing product) × (Publish or Save as Draft). Three are checked imperatively in `save()` before any request is made — at least three photos, at least one pricing tier, and at least one turnaround option — and, confirmed this run, all three apply identically regardless of which button was clicked; there is no 'allow an incomplete draft' path today. The rest come from the Zod schema — name, slug, short description and category are required, unit prices cannot be negative, tier quantities must be at least one, and stock figures cannot be negative when inventory tracking is on — and, also confirmed this run, these now genuinely block the submit in every one of the four combinations, including editing an already-published product. The backend independently enforces the same three-photo and one-tier minimums (`Field(min_length=3)` / `Field(min_length=1)`) and rejects a slug that another product already uses with a 409.

Deleting is not what it sounds like, but as of this run's earlier pass, it is at least now telling the truth about that. `DELETE /admin/products/{id}` archives the product — it sets `status: archived` and `is_active: false`, and no longer deletes its media from storage first — and both dialogs that trigger it now describe that outcome the same way.

sections.heading: User flow
sections.body_markdown:
A member of staff signs in at `/login` and lands on the dashboard, then opens **Products** from the Catalogue section of the sidebar. The list arrives with every product in the catalogue, newest first, and can now genuinely be searched, sorted and filtered by status.

Clicking **Add Product** opens the empty form. They type the product name — *Premium Business Cards*, say — and watch the Slug field fill itself in as they type. They add a one-line short description, pick a category, and drag in three photos; the line above the dropzone counts down from *3 more photos required — minimum 3.* to *Minimum of 3 photos met (3/8).* The pricing tiers arrive pre-populated with a sensible five-tier ladder, and they mark one of them as the best-value tier with a star. Opening the Inventory section, they switch on tracking and enter a stock level, which the form immediately summarises back to them as *500 units in stock.*

**Publish Product** saves it. A *Product created* toast confirms, and they are returned to the list where the new product is now the first row — active, in its category, with its lowest tier price under 'From'.

Editing follows the same shape in reverse: the row menu's **Edit** opens the populated form, changes are confirmed with **Save Changes** and a *Product updated* toast, and reassigning the category is visible back on the list immediately. If a required field is accidentally cleared along the way — the product name, the category, the short description — neither Save Changes nor Save as Draft goes through silently: an inline message appears under the empty field and nothing is sent to the server, whether the product is brand new or already live. Retiring a product is done from the row menu's **Delete**, which asks for confirmation, reports `"<name>" archived`, and — now — actually keeps the product's photos in storage while it waits to be restored.

sections.heading: Annotated screenshots
sections.body_markdown:
The screenshots below trace the main journey, the moments where the application pushes back on bad input, and the required-field/draft-vs-publish follow-up pass. They are drawn from five capture passes — the happy path, the error paths, the list controls, the form edges, and the required-field unselect suite — which is why the file paths differ.

Note that screenshots are gitignored, so these render as filename references rather than images outside a local checkout.

sections.heading: Test results & coverage
sections.body_markdown:
**91 of 91 steps passed**, across two passes. Coverage was deliberately exhaustive rather than representative: the first pass found five real defects (four fixed, one flagged for a modelling decision); a second, narrower pass specifically targeting required-field validation and the draft-vs-publish distinction found three of the earlier findings had since been fixed, and surfaced two brand-new issues.

### Fixed in the first pass

**1. The product form's validation never ran at all.** The Publish and Save-as-Draft buttons called `save()` directly and read `form.getValues()`, so `zodResolver` never executed and `formState.errors` was permanently empty. Publishing a blank form (with the three photos that *were* checked) created a real product with an empty name, an empty slug, no category and `status: active` — live in the storefront catalogue. Both buttons now submit through `form.handleSubmit`.

**2. A duplicate slug reported the wrong reason.** The backend answers a slug collision with a 409 and the message `Slug '<slug>' is already in use`, but the form only surfaced the server's text for a 422, so the admin saw the generic *Failed to save product*.

**3. Opening any product for editing silently rewrote its slug.** The auto-slug effect in `BasicInfoSection` fired on mount as well as on typing, so loading an existing product replaced its stored slug with one derived from its name — with `shouldDirty: false`, so not even the 'Unsaved changes' warning appeared. Auto-derivation is now create-mode only and stops once the slug is hand-edited.

**4. Missing numeric bounds, and a missing not-found state.** A negative unit price, a zero tier quantity and a negative stock level could all be saved; they are now rejected with visible messages. Separately, `/products/{id}` for an id that does not exist rendered the *create* form under an 'Edit Product' heading, complete with a Publish button. It now shows a proper not-found state.

### Fixed and re-confirmed since (verified this pass, not by an agent)

**5. `edge-04` — the Active filter used to return a product badged Draft.** `status` and `is_active` were two independently-settable sources of truth for one fact and had diverged in the live database. `status` is now canonical: the admin routes derive `is_active` from it, `GET /admin/products` gained a real `status` parameter, and the list's status filter now sends it. Re-run this pass: every row returned under the Active filter is genuinely badged Active.

**6. The search box and sort headers were fully rendered controls wired to nothing.** `setSearch` was an empty stub and the sort headers had no backend parameter to call. Both are now real: `GET /admin/products` accepts `q` (case-insensitive partial match on name/slug/short_description) and a combined `sort` parameter (e.g. `min_price_asc`), and the list UI calls both. Confirmed this pass: searching a product's own name returns only matching rows, and clicking the Product column header sorts the current page ascending by name.

**7. The delete/archive dialogs contradicted each other and the backend.** The edit form's dialog said the action was permanent; the list's said it was reversible; the backend used to delete every image and video from storage before archiving, so neither was fully true. The edit form's dialog copy now matches the list's, and archiving no longer deletes media — so the shared, correct claim ('archived and hidden... can be restored') is now actually true both ways.

### New findings from the required-field / draft-vs-publish pass

This pass added one new spec covering all four combinations of (create a new product / update an existing one) × (Publish / Save as Draft), clearing the Name, Category, and Short Description one at a time, and separately exercising the pricing-tier and photo-count guards under Save as Draft specifically (the earlier suite had only ever exercised those two guards via Publish).

**Confirmed working correctly in every one of the four combinations:** clearing Name, Category, or Short Description on a brand-new product, and — critically — on an *already-published, live* product, blocks both Publish and Save as Draft with the correct inline message and no request sent. Editing an existing product and accidentally clearing a required field, then clicking either save button, does not corrupt or partially save that product; reloading afterward shows the original name, description, category, and all five pricing tiers exactly as they were.

**Finding A — Save as Draft cannot save an incomplete product, and this is a decision, not (yet) a bug.** The same non-empty checks that block Publish when there are zero photos or zero pricing tiers block Save as Draft identically. An admin who wants to save partial progress — pricing not decided yet, photos not shot yet — gets the same hard stop as trying to go fully live. This may be exactly the intended behaviour, or it may not be; this run only establishes that the current behaviour is *consistent* between the two buttons, not that it's the *right* behaviour for what 'draft' should mean here.

**Finding B — removing a photo from an already-published product deletes it from storage immediately, regardless of whether anything is ever saved.** `MediaSection`'s remove button calls the delete-media API the instant it's clicked, for any uploaded image, with no distinction between one added seconds ago and one that's been live on the storefront for months. The save-time guard ('At least 3 photos are required') does correctly stop the product's database record from being updated with too few images — but that protection only covers the record. The photo files themselves are already gone from storage the moment 'Remove image' is clicked, proved this run via three intercepted, successful delete requests fired before any Save button was even touched. An admin who removes photos while editing a live product and then either hits this guard or simply navigates away is left with a product whose stored image references no longer point at anything real. This is exactly the kind of silent, already-published-product corruption this pass was designed to look for, and it's a genuine defect, not a design question.

**Finding C — the Category dropdown can visually show blank after a hard page reload, even when the real category is intact.** Confirmed via a direct, read-only check against the backend that the underlying data never changed. The cause is a loading-order race: the category list only starts loading once the product itself has finished loading, and if the matching option isn't in the dropdown yet at the moment the form first renders, the browser leaves the dropdown on its blank placeholder and never revisits that decision — even after the real options arrive. A normal in-app click from the list to Edit doesn't trigger this (the category list is already loaded by then); a hard reload or a direct link does. No data is lost, but it can look like it is.

### What was *not* exercised

- **RBAC.** `products.view/create/edit/delete` gate the API, but the products feature calls `usePermissions()` nowhere, so a view-only role would see enabled controls that 403 on submit. Proving that needs a second seeded staff account, which this run did not create.
- **Bulk actions.** None exist — `ProductsTable` enables neither row selection nor a bulk toolbar, though `DataTable` supports both.
- **The turnaround-options guard.** Its error message can never appear: the section renders a fixed Standard/Express/Rush trio with no remove control.
- **Cross-UI price agreement.** The admin list's 'From' price and the storefront's are computed by two independent rules; confirming they diverge needs both halves in one pass.

sections.heading: Accessibility
sections.body_markdown:
This run both measured and substantially improved the product screens' accessibility, and the second pass re-exercised the same components (all 20 field-clear/restore cycles, plus 3 hard reloads) without surfacing anything new. Every figure below is an axe-core count taken per navigation, so each finding belongs to the route rather than to a single interaction.

**Fixed in the first pass, and still clean:**

| Rule | Severity | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| `label` — form elements without a programmatic label | critical | 21 nodes | 2 |
| `select-name` — select with no accessible name | critical | 5 nodes | 0 |
| `button-name` — buttons with no discernible text | critical | 27 nodes | 2 |
| `label-title-only` — labelled only via `title` | serious | 11 nodes | 0 |
| `aria-toggle-field-name` — unnamed switches | serious | 3 nodes | 0 |
| `empty-table-header` | minor | 1 node | 0 |

The `label` finding deserves a note, because it was corroborated from outside the scanner: while writing the test suite, `getByLabel()` matched nothing anywhere on the product form, and every single field had to be located by an XPath lookup off its label's text. Labels are now paired via `useId()`, and the dense field-array tables use an `aria-label` naming both the column and the row, e.g. *Quantity for pricing tier 3*.

**Resolved since the first pass:** `link-name` (serious, 1 node on `/products`) was a symptom, not a cause — the product-name link of the empty-name row that the (now-fixed) validation bypass allowed to be created. This pass confirms the underlying cause is actually gone: 20 separate attempts to save a product with an empty name, across both create and update mode and both Publish and Save as Draft, produced zero nameless rows.

**Still left open:**

- `color-contrast` (serious, 12–27 nodes on every admin route including the dashboard) — untouched on purpose. This is a design-token decision spanning the whole admin theme, not a product-catalogue bug.
- `heading-order` on the product form, where the collapsible `<h3>` section headers sit directly under the page `<h1>`, plus 2 residual `label` and 2 residual `button-name` nodes outside this feature's own components.
- The login page's own `landmark-one-main`, `region` and `page-has-heading-one` findings, out of scope for this feature.

**Coverage caveat: automated scan only — manual/screen-reader review still needed.** Automated scanning typically catches only 30–40% of real accessibility issues, so a reduced count here is progress, not compliance.

sections.heading: Performance
sections.body_markdown:
**No performance numbers were captured for this feature, and that was a deliberate choice rather than an omission.**

The admin panel keeps its access token in memory only (Zustand, never `localStorage`), so the capture harness cannot restore a live session into the context Lighthouse audits. A post-login checkpoint gets bounced to `/login`, which means any figure it produced would describe the login page while being labelled as the products page — the `url_mismatch` failure mode recorded in this app's own configuration notes. Publishing numbers that measure the wrong page is worse than publishing none.

Three latency observations are worth recording anyway, as leads for a future measured audit rather than as results:

- Opening a product for editing, and reloading it mid-edit, both sit on a loading skeleton for a few seconds — observed repeatedly in this pass's required-field suite, which reloads the same product's edit page three times in a row.
- Every filter, search or sort change on the catalogue list refetches from scratch and drops the table to skeleton rows before repainting. That is unremarkable at 21 products; it is now more consequential than before, since search and sort are real operations an admin will actually reach for, not dead controls.
- Any future measurement here must come from a production build. Anything captured from the Next.js dev server is only useful as a run-over-run baseline, never as a shippable score.

sections.heading: Recommendations & future improvements
sections.body_markdown:
Ordered by severity, carrying the analysis's rankings unchanged.

**High — stop photo removal from deleting an already-persisted image from storage before any save succeeds.** `MediaSection.removeImage()` calls the delete API the instant 'Remove image' is clicked, for any image, new or already-published. Either defer the actual deletion until the surrounding save genuinely succeeds — tracking removed-but-unsaved keys the way `cleanupNewUploads()` already tracks added-but-unsaved ones — or make it unmistakably clear in the UI that removal is immediate and independent of Save. The save-time guard currently gives false confidence: it protects the database record, not the files.

**Medium — decide, deliberately, what 'Save as Draft' is allowed to do.** It is currently blocked by the exact same photo/pricing-tier completeness checks as Publish, on both new and existing products. That may be correct, or it may be blocking a legitimate 'save my partial progress' workflow — this run only confirms the behaviour is consistent, not that it's intended.

**Medium — fix the Category dropdown's post-reload blank-render bug.** Either start loading the category list in parallel with the product (rather than only once the form mounts), or make the `<select>` a controlled component so a later arrival of the real options can still correct the displayed value. No data is at risk, but an admin can be misled into thinking a correctly-set category is missing.

**Medium — finish the accessibility pass** on the product form's `heading-order` and the two residual `button-name` nodes outside this feature's own components.

**Medium — tell the admin when the image dropzone discards files** over the eight-image cap, matching the clarity of the minimum-photo counter directly above it.

**Low — cover the RBAC paths** with a seeded view-only staff account, and add `usePermissions()` gating to the products feature so a role without `products.edit` does not see enabled controls that will 403. The content, staff and shipping features already establish the pattern.

**Low — reconcile the two 'From' price rules** (admin list vs. storefront), or document which is canonical.
